newsitem.title: CHINA: China retrieves scientific research satellite.
newsitem.headline: China retrieves scientific research satellite.

text.p: China, reeling from a string of space setbacks, scored a modest victory on Monday when it successfully retrieved a scientific research satellite.
The satellite for scientific exploration and technological experiments returned to earth after a pre-set orbit of 15 days, the Xinhua news agency said.
The satellite landed in the southwestern province of Sichuan, Xinhua said. It was launched on October 20 using a Long March 2D rocket.

The Xi'an Satellite Surveying and Controlling Centre monitored and controlled the satellite for 15 days, during which period an exploration and orbit-changing experiment was conducted achieving "expected" results, Xinhua said.

Chinese experts said data acquired through the exploration and technological experiment were of vital importance to national land surveys, geological and seismological forecasting, mineral prospecting, agricultural and forestry development, environmental protection and national defence, Xinhua said.
China has successfully launched 17 retrievable satellites since 1975 and retrieved 16 of them, Xinhua said.
China's space industry, once much admired for its bargain prices and strong track record of launch successes, has been plagued by problems in recent years.
In August, a domestic communications satellite launched aboard a Long March 3 rocket from Xichang in Sichuan province failed to reach its proper orbit.
In February, a Long March 3B carrying an Intel satellite veered wildly seconds after lift-off before exploding in mid-air near the Xichang space centre.

China said six people were killed, 57 injured and 80 homes destroyed, but video footage smuggled out of China by an Israeli scientist showed dozens of levelled buildings and suggested the casualties were higher.
In January 1995, a Long March 2E rocket blew up, killing a family of six in a rain of debris and destroying the Hughes-built Apstar 2 satellite it was carrying.
